status.en: 133 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 29% fewer than the week before, most of them in Islamabad, Kabul and Balochistan.
status.nb: 133 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 29 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Islamabad, Kabul og Balochistan.

summary.en: There were 153 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 24% fewer than the previous week, concentrated in Islamabad, Kabul and Balochistan, and 24 of these were covered by two or more outlets. The UCDP recorded 1,794 battle‑related deaths in 2024. Recent developments include the killing of dozens of terrorists in operations across Barkhan, Tank and Bannu, the death of an election commission director general, the discovery of heroin near the Punjab border, the detention of Afghans on an illegal Herat‑Iran crossing, reports of child soldiers recruited by the Taliban, and ongoing diplomatic and security tensions between Pakistan and Afghanistan.
summary.nb: Det ble rapportert 153 væpnede hendelser de siste syv dagene, 24 % færre enn uken før, konsentrert i Islamabad, Kabul og Balochistan, og 24 av dem ble dekket av to eller flere kilder. UCDP registrerte 1 794 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024. Nylige utviklinger inkluderer drap på flere titalls terrorister i operasjoner i Barkhan, Tank og Bannu, døden til en valgkommisjonsdirektør, funnet av heroin ved grensen i Punjab, arrestasjon av afghanere på en ulovlig Herat‑Iran‑rute, rapporter om at Taliban rekrutterer barnesoldater, samt pågående diplomatiske og sikkerhetsmessige spenninger mellom Pakistan og Afghanistan.

background.title: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
background.extract: Since 2004, an insurgency has been fought in the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by Islamist militant groups such as the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Jundallah, Lashkar-e-Islam (LeI), the Tehreek-e-Nafaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi (TNSM), Al-Qaeda, and their Central Asian allies such as the Islamic State – Khorasan Province (ISKP), Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, East Turkistan Movement, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Ittihad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, and elements of organised crime. Before being transformed into an insurgency in 2017, the conflict was a war.
